bounds_and_contract_differences: EquityHistorical and EtfHistorical accept one validated symbol, explicit start_date/end_date, and interval=1d only. The public Cboe history query lists 1m and 1d and permits multiple symbols; the official All Access endpoint documents historical end-of-day snapshots from 2011, not a one-minute bar aggregation endpoint. The local adapter therefore does not synthesize 1m bars and does not fetch an unbounded default window.

Daily history windows are limited locally to 28 calendar days and at most 20 trading dates; each query first reads the bounded trading-day range and then fetches one end-of-day quote collection per trading date. The adapter fails closed if the API returns more than 20 dates; it does not silently truncate. The current New York market date is not accepted for daily history, matching the official historical-request rule.

The official underlying-quotes schema says SIP subscription is required for delayed bid/ask/size and OHLC fields; without the subscription several fields may be null. CboeEquityQuote preserves unavailable nullable fields as null. CboeEquityHistorical's public OHLC contract requires numeric values, so a history row with missing required OHLC fails closed instead of fabricating prices.

EquityQuote accepts one symbol and a date extension (default: current New York date); the official underlying-quotes endpoint requires date and seq_no, so the adapter explicitly sends seq_no=0. Public model fields unavailable from this endpoint remain null. The documented Cboe public query allows multiple symbols; this local adapter is deliberately single-symbol and does not silently discard additional symbols.

EquitySearch query is optional and defaults to the complete official reference/symbols collection; is_symbol defaults false. Filtering is local and case-insensitive. The Cboe public row also contains dpm_name and post_station; the official symbols API publishes only name/company_name, so those two fields are null. The adapter rejects malformed rows and excessive response size rather than truncating.

OptionsChains requires one symbol and defaults date to the current New York market date. Optional root, option_type, min_expiry, max_expiry, min_strike, and max_strike are sent using the documented source query names. The official route returns a list of SymbolWithOptions objects, so the adapter selects exactly one requested symbol and maps its option collection into the public column-oriented output. More than 5,000 contracts is an explicit error, not a partial result.

All All Access requests require an externally provisioned CBOE_LIVEVOL_ACCESS_TOKEN bearer token. The adapter does not perform OAuth token exchange, persist responses, or claim storage/redistribution rights. Source docs identify point-based delayed API calls and SIP subscription requirements for some quote fields; this code has bounded RequestBudget/shared-host controls but no dedicated hourly point or call ledger and does not claim an exact provider quota.

official_facts: Cboe's VIX historical page explicitly links the VIX daily CSV for 1990-present and seven other volatility-index CSVs: VVIX, VIX9D, OVX, GVZ, VXAPL, VXAZN, and VXEEM.

The VIX capture is 473584 bytes with SHA-256 51ea1e59bfeaf400f6816300c39145df5e3fb437e7c60bdb8ca2178f8c96f436 and header DATE,OPEN,HIGH,LOW,CLOSE. The other seven officially linked CSVs were also fetched into bounded investigation captures; all returned HTTP 200, text/csv, and complete bodies below the 4 MiB capture limit.

Observed strict headers: VVIX, OVX, and GVZ use DATE plus their same-named index value; VIX9D, VXAPL, VXAZN, and VXEEM use DATE,OPEN,HIGH,LOW,CLOSE. The parser maps one-value files to close and OHLC files to their matching fields; all observed files have no volume column, so volume and the three options-volume extension fields are null.

The page describes daily closing values. The adapter preserves the values as published without scaling and retains each CSV's final published row. Whether that final row always satisfies a separate latest-trading-day freshness rule remains unresolved.
missing: General index-symbol and regional coverage beyond the eight listed volatility indices, plus the separate older VXO file mapping.
